recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Future work should treat changes to this artifact as ServiceRequest-specific unless a new work-group decision explicitly reopens the combined-resource boundary or naming question.
issue_request: FHIR-11119 was Published with resolution Persuasive. It asked whether ProcedureRequest and DiagnosticRequest should remain separate, identified misaligned parallel element names, and resolved to combine DiagnosticRequest and ProcedureRequest using the broader ProcedureRequest name with a superset of both resources' elements.
initial_application: The issue was applied by historical [#11119] commits, especially e9a85998b0dbe25b03abd0045bfa30e67ce56b36, ad1050b14bb5ec8a8c29b5448d991ef09bca5b2a, 37f014c2b7d4e85beace7c89e30b0308975d91ae, 6798563c36e0143ed1ca837b2a9bd1ee22254d97, and 2fa71284c7cb0518c0d71318cc883f828b33c1bc. Those commits removed DiagnosticRequest from active build configuration, deleted the DiagnosticRequest source folder, moved diagnostic examples and terminology into ProcedureRequest, and updated ProcedureRequest narrative and element definitions. FHIR-13867 later renamed ProcedureRequest to ServiceRequest in commit 06bd9f6ffe08096694a3424721006e5fdcd82d3a.
additional_context: The current build scope is ServiceRequest. source/fhir.ini actively lists servicerequest=ServiceRequest, records DiagnosticOrder as subsumed into ServiceRequest and ProcedureRequest as merged into ServiceRequest, and preserves old-name mappings such as scheduled to occurrence and orderedOn to authoredOn. Current ServiceRequest source describes diagnostic investigations, treatments, and operations; includes diagnostic request as an alias; and carries #11119 committee notes across aligned merged elements. Zulip discussion confirms the merge was intentional and announced as a breaking STU3 change, while Confluence searches found no contrary record. Related follow-up issues are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. DiagnosticRequest and ProcedureRequest are no longer independent active current resources, and their combined successor ServiceRequest already covers diagnostic and procedure service requests with aligned request-pattern element names. Remaining ProcedureRequest or DiagnosticRequest strings are historical notes, migration metadata, old-type terminology, or unrelated example comments rather than active conformance source needing correction for FHIR-11119.
